context.guidance: Do not write Personal Data or Authentication Secrets to localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies or outbound headers beyond what the session strictly needs. Keep identity in an opaque session identifier held server-side, and keep only non-Personal Data preferences in the browser. Where a value must be held client-side, protect it as Rule 6(1)(a) requires.

value.fix: Don't put the auth token in localStorage. Any script running on the page can read localStorage, so an XSS bug would let an attacker steal the token. Have the server issue an opaque session identifier and send it as a cookie with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict (or Lax) set. Keep the token-to-identity mapping on the server, and remove `localStorage.setItem('token', authentication.token)`. Client requests should then authenticate through the cookie by using `credentials: 'include'` / `withCredentials: true`, not by reading a stored token and adding an Authorization header. Add CSRF protection, such as a SameSite cookie plus a CSRF token on requests that change state. If a «SECRET» truly has to stay on the client, keep it only in memory (for example a closure or state variable), make it short-lived, refresh it through an HttpOnly refresh cookie, and never write it to localStorage, sessionStorage or a script-readable cookie. On logout, delete any existing 'token' entry with `localStorage.removeItem('token')` and invalidate the session on the server.
